payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. Its gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte. An independent audit retracted the original 12,000-cycle claim; the corrected governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold.

payload.text:
The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. Its measured gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, while projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.

An independent teardown audit retracted the original 12,000-cycle claim, attributing it to un-normalized depth-of-discharge reporting. Although the audit text contains a conflicting interim measurement, it identifies 8,400 cycles as the corrected, governing cycle-life figure.
